title: Finish and troubleshoot the project
summary: Check the complete C# and Oracle project, fix common setup errors and understand what needs to change before a local API becomes a public service.
introduction: You now have the pieces of a real data app: a browser, a C# API and an Oracle table. Finishing means checking how they work together, knowing how to find a problem, and keeping the local learning project separate from a public service.
learningObjectives: Trace a request through all three parts
Use error clues to check the right setting
Explain why GitHub Pages hosts lessons but not this backend

items: Add one made-up book through the optional browser page or PowerShell.
Read that same row in SQL*Plus.
Mark it as read with PUT and request it again.
Restart the API and check that the row is still in Oracle.
Delete only the practice row you added.

blocks.text: If the row survives an API restart, you have seen what a database is for. The data does not live only in a temporary C# list or in browser storage.
Use the error as a clue

rows: Install the SDK and open a new terminal.
Run the secret helper for the supplied project.
ORA-12541 or a connection refused message
Check that the Oracle listener is running and the host and port are correct.
Check the actual application service, such as FREEPDB1.
Check the reading_app username and its password.
Check which user and service you connected to and whether its book table exists.
Read the validation problem and correct the request body or numeric ID.
Check the page origin, development CORS setting and API address.
blocks.caption: Start with the part named by the failure

blocks.text: The API sends a general HTTP 500 problem if database work fails. Read the API terminal for the cause, but do not share passwords or a full connection string when asking for help. Fix one thing at a time and repeat the same test.

items: A complete local learning API with list, read, create, update and delete actions.
Input checks, named Oracle parameters and explicit write transactions.
A small browser page for listing and adding books.
Database setup files and a repeatable API test script.

blocks.text: GitHub Pages can host this tutorial and static files. It cannot run dotnet or an Oracle database. A public backend needs a separate host that runs .NET and can reach Oracle. Keep credentials on that host, use HTTPS, and choose who is allowed to read and change records.

Before storing real data, add suitable access control, a limited database runtime account, backups, request limits and a plan for checking errors. Add pagination before a book list becomes large. The sample intentionally returns the whole small list and has no sign-in.

Write a short note explaining what happens after POST /api/books. Name the controller, request model, repository, table, commit and HTTP 201 reply. Then show a friend one valid request and one invalid request.

Keep learning with the [C# tutorial](/tutorials/csharp), [ASP.NET Core tutorial](/tutorials/aspnet-core), [Oracle Database tutorial](/tutorials/oracle-database) and [combined learning path](/learning-paths/dotnet-oracle-backend).
